document.title: Host Control: let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
document.summary: Adds Host Control end to end: the `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` client and plugin API, the `vitadeck-host-companion` CLI with built-in `core` and `systemStats` plugins that installs custom `.vdplugin` packages, SDK CLI support to build those packages with a Deck App or standalone, the native link listener and link store with a Shell Host Control screen, and a `host-control` example Deck App.
document.why: Máté asked for the three Host Control slices, shaped so later Deck Apps can send keys, read sensors and set controls, act like a Stream Deck, drive several machines on different OSes, and show a T3 Code dashboard ([session](source:s5)).

sources.title: Host Control slice A: wire contract and SDK client
sources.gist: JSON-over-HTTP contract, error codes, typed registry, `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` client, shared fixtures.

sources.title: Host Control slice B: Host Companion CLI
sources.gist: Private companion package with `start` and `link`, config file, peer check, node:test suite.

sources.title: Host Control slice C: native link listener and Shell Host Control screen
sources.gist: Shared HTTP parsing, LAN address in platform, link listener and store, native getter, Shell entry and screen, C harness.

sources.label: PR #144
sources.gist: One PR for all three slices; plugins instead of a flat catalogue; several links; demo Deck App.

sources.label: T3 Code session · Oct 28
sources.gist: Implement all three issues; target use cases shape the design but are not built now; the backend extension model is left to the agent; add a demo Deck App.

lookFor: [#109](source:s1) asks for flat command names and an internal `defineHostCommands`. Every request instead names a `plugin`, and `defineHostPlugin` and `command` are public, because the [session](source:s5) left the extension model open and [PR #144](source:s4) chose plugins.

[#109](source:s1) and [#111](source:s3) name the getter `nativeGetHostControlUrl()` and one stored link in `host-control-link.json`. At head `nativeGetHostControlLinks()` returns a JSON array of up to 4 links in `host-control-links.json`, keyed by a new companion `id` in the link payload, so one Deck App can reach several machines ([session](source:s5)).
[#109](source:s1) asks for a new `test:sdk` script. At head the SDK host-control tests run under the existing `test:cli` glob; no source gives a reason.
[#110](source:s2) keeps one `vita` in the companion config. At head `vitas` is an array, since several Vitas can link one companion.
[#111](source:s3) describes a `Forget link` action. At head Cross on a linked computer row forgets that one link at once.
Credentials stay deferred, as ADR 0004 says, so the built-in plugins only read information; custom plugins can act on the computer and run with the user's permissions.

Not true at head: `@vitadeck/host-companion` is still `private: true`, so a project from `create --host-plugin` or `--host-plugin-only` cannot `npm install` its companion devDependency until the package is published.

groups.title: Wire contract and SDK client
groups.why: Slice A: the contract every other piece speaks, and the client Deck Apps call ([#109](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `createHostClient` in `client.ts` turns a `defineHostPlugin` registry from `plugin.ts` into typed methods that POST the `protocol.ts` envelope and map every failure to a `HostResult`, while `plugin.ts` also gives plugin authors `implementHostPlugin`, `HostCommandError` and the `HostPluginManifest` contract, and `system-stats.ts` holds the built-in `systemStats` registry.
lookFor: `implementHostPlugin` and `HostCommandError` sit in the same subpath Deck Apps bundle; rolldown tree-shakes them from apps that never call them.

groups.title: Host Companion: vitadeck-host-companion, built-ins and plugin packages
groups.why: Slice B: the long-lived listener on the computer that performs the link and runs plugin commands ([#110](source:s2)), installable on its own and loading plugins from `.vdplugin` packages ([session](source:s5)).
groups.summary: `cli.ts` runs `start`, which serves `POST /command` from `server.ts` over `core`, the built-in `systemStats` and every `.vdplugin` package `plugin.ts` loads from `~/.vitadeck/plugins/` or `--plugin` (reloading them on change through `setPlugins`), `install`/`remove`, which unpack and delete those packages, and `link`, which POSTs the link payload from `link.ts` and records the Vita in `config.ts`; `rolldown.config.mjs` bundles it with the SDK into one dependency-free `vitadeck-host-companion` bin.
lookFor: Subtle: `HostCommandError` is matched by `name` and wire `code`, not `instanceof`, because each package bundles its own copy of the class.
A package's entry is imported as `<file URL>?v=<sha256 of the entry>`, so a rebuilt entry loads fresh but a rebuild that changes only `files/` keeps the cached module; plugins read `files/` per call.

`install` stages into `.install-*` inside the plugins folder, validates, then renames to `<id>.vdplugin`; the extractor refuses several roots, backslashes, empty segments and `..`, ignores `__MACOSX/`, and keeps no file modes.
Paths resolve against `INIT_CWD` only under the repo's own `host-companion` script; elsewhere against the working directory.
On macOS `systemStats` counts free, inactive and speculative `vm_stat` pages as available; elsewhere it uses `os.freemem()`, which reads `MemAvailable` on Linux.

groups.title: SDK CLI: build Host Plugin packages, with or without a Deck App
groups.why: Authors keep a plugin in a Deck App's repo or on its own, and ship it as a `.vdplugin` package like the `.vdapp` ([session](source:s5)).
groups.summary: `hostPlugin: { entry, files? }` in `vitadeck.config.json` makes `build` bundle the entry into a staged `<slug>.vdplugin` folder with `manifest.json` and `files/`, swap it in and zip it, `entry` becomes optional so a plugin-only project builds and `dev`s alone, and `create --host-plugin` / `--host-plugin-only` scaffold the two layouts from the `host-plugin` and `host-plugin-only` templates.
lookFor: A failed plugin build leaves the previous `<slug>.vdplugin` in place: the package is written to `<slug>.vdplugin.tmp` and renamed over the old folder only after everything succeeds.
`vitadeck dev` takes a Runtime Upload URL exactly when the project has a Deck App `entry`; a plugin-only project rebuilds on save without one.

The standalone template takes `@vitadeck/sdk` as a peer and dev dependency and exports `./host/plugin.ts`, so a Deck App installing it from git or npm shares its own SDK; `copy-templates.ts` rewrites `workspace:*` in every template's dependency fields.
The scaffolded plugin id is the project slug, so two projects scaffolded with the same name collide on one companion.

groups.title: Shared native helpers moved out of upload and storage
groups.why: The link listener reuses Runtime Upload's request reading, the manifest's jimp parsing, and Deck App Storage's safe file replace, so [#111](source:s3) moves them where both callers reach them.
groups.summary: Upload's HTTP helpers move to `src/net/http.c`, its LAN address detection to `src/platform/lan_address_*`, jimp and JSON escaping to `src/core/json.c`, and Deck App Storage's replace-file logic to `vd_replace_file` in `src/core/util.c`.
lookFor: A Deck App Storage write that fails to move the old file aside now reports "Could not write Deck App Storage." instead of "Could not replace Deck App Storage."; the `.tmp` and `.bak` names stay the same, so a backup left by an older build is still recovered.
`http_read_request` always NUL-terminates the body it returns, so the link parser can hand it to jimp; Runtime Upload ignores the extra byte.

groups.title: Link listener, store and native getter
groups.why: Slice C: VitaDeck accepts a link only while asked, keeps it across restarts, and lets Deck Apps read it ([#111](source:s3)).
groups.summary: `listener.c` accepts one `POST /link` on 8798+, `link.c` validates it and stores up to 4 links through `vd_replace_file`, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks` in `jslib/host_control.c` hands the list to the SDK client.

groups.title: Shell Host Control entry and screen
groups.why: The user reads the link address and forgets links on the Vita ([#111](source:s3)).
groups.summary: A Host Control row after Upload opens `VD_SHELL_HOST_CONTROL`, which starts the listener, shows the address, status and linked computers, and stops the listener on a link, Circle, Start or shutdown.
lookFor: After a successful link the listener has stopped, so the screen swaps the `vitadeck-host-companion link` hint for "go Back and open Host Control again"; linking a second computer needs that round trip.

groups.title: host-control example Deck App
groups.why: The [session](source:s5) asked for a demo Deck App showcasing Host Control.
groups.summary: `App.tsx` polls `linkedHosts()` and each host's built-in `systemStats.read`, imported from the SDK, lists the computers with live CPU, and shows the selected one's capabilities, gauges and an Echo round trip.
lookFor: After a `timeout` the demo polls that computer every 30 s instead of every second, because the native fetch keeps running up to its 30 s curl cap after the SDK gives up at 5 s.

groups.title: Glossary, ADR, agent skills and checks
groups.why: Docs that the new design made inaccurate are fixed in place, and the companion tests join the `fast` tier ([#110](source:s2)).

commits.subject: docs(skills): add vitadeck-host-control and cover Host Control in the others
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The new public skill covers running and linking the Host Companion, calling
plugins from a Deck App, writing plugins with a Deck App or standalone, the
author loop, installing .vdplugin packages, and error codes. deck-app-init
learns --host-plugin and --host-plugin-only, manual-testing gets a Host
Control section, vdapp-upload says .vdplugin.zip goes to the computer, and
build lists the companion bundle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: test(sdk): pin the standalone plugin's peer SDK and exclusive create flags
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: docs(sdk): say which SDK copy a linked standalone plugin uses
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(sdk): standalone plugins take the SDK as a peer dependency
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App and the plugin it depends on now share one @vitadeck/sdk, so
command result types survive and the host-control code is bundled once.
dev refuses a URL in a plugin-only project, create refuses --host-plugin with
--host-plugin-only, and --no-zip help covers both archives.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(sdk): Host Plugins can be authored without a Deck App
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A vitadeck.config.json may have hostPlugin without an entry: build then
writes only the .vdplugin package and zip, and dev rebuilds them without a
Runtime Upload URL. `vitadeck create <name> --host-plugin-only` scaffolds such
a project, whose package.json exports host/plugin.ts so any Deck App can
depend on it. Template package.json files all get published versions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(sdk): build the plugin package beside the old one and swap it in
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-control): a broken plugin build keeps the last good package
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Bundle before replacing the package folder, copy linked files as files, and
require hostPlugin.files to be a folder. The companion ignores __MACOSX/ in
archives and points a --plugin .zip at install. Docs say the zip keeps no
file modes and that files/ is read per call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): a Deck App's plugin ships as a .vdplugin package and zip
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion
installs archives or folders into ~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin, loads the
entry by file URL so it finds its files through import.meta.url, and watches
package folders recursively.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): --plugin takes a directory, so the scaffold survives a renamed app
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): allow plugin ids as long as a package slug
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): rename the plugin's module copy into place
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): install renames the plugin into place
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): load plugins from file copies, resolve paths from the cwd
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A bundled CommonJS dependency calls createRequire(import.meta.url), which a
data: URL cannot satisfy; plugins now load from a content-hashed .mjs copy.
Paths resolve against the working directory except under the repo's own
`host-companion` script, so a Deck App's `host` script works from anywhere.
Plugin ids may start with a digit, and watcher errors are logged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): built-in plugins, .vdplugin files, vitadeck-host-companion
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App now keeps its own Host Control Plugin in its project: `hostPlugin`
in vitadeck.config.json makes `vitadeck build` bundle the implementation into
one self-contained <slug>.vdplugin, and `vitadeck create --host-plugin`
scaffolds it. Users install that file with `vitadeck-host-companion install`;
the companion reloads installed and --plugin files when they change.

systemStats moves into the companion as a built-in, with its registry in
@vitadeck/sdk/host-control next to implementHostPlugin and HostCommandError.
The companion is a dependency-free bundled package with the
vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): reject unlinked peers before reading their body
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-control): close a connection accepted while the listener stops
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-control): show how to link another computer after a link; help before commands
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-control): review fixes for polling backoff, result spread, and listener stop
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: feat(examples): Host Control demo Deck App, docs, and agent-check
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Adds the host-control example, the Host Control glossary terms, rewrites
ADR 0004 for plugins and several links, adds the companion tests to the
fast tier, and makes system-stats read macOS memory like Activity Monitor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): Host Control Link listener, store, getter, and Shell screen
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Slice C of ADR 0004. VitaDeck keeps up to four Host Control Links in <data root>/host-control-links.json and exposes them to Deck Apps through nativeGetHostControlLinks. The Shell Host Control Screen starts a listener on 8798-8807 that accepts one POST /link, and Cross forgets a linked computer.

Upload's HTTP helpers move to src/net/http, LAN address detection to src/platform/lan_address_*, jimp's implementation and the JSON skip and escape helpers to src/core/json, and Deck App Storage's Vita-safe file replace to src/core/util so the link store reuses it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-companion): Host Companion CLI and system-stats plugin
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Adds @vitadeck/host-companion (start, link, implementHostPlugin, config) and
the first-party read-only @vitadeck/host-plugin-system-stats plugin, with
node:test coverage that replays the Host Control fixtures against the server.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(sdk): typecheck and lint the Host Control tests
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The SDK tsconfig did not include test/*.ts, so oxlint's type-aware rules saw
every host-control.test.ts value as an error type and pnpm lint failed. Include
the tests and fix the lint findings in the client and its tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
